The tool searches, screens, reads and cites across hundreds of legal sources for each question. It is free to use for one month, with up to 25 searches per user. The launch addresses a familiar constraint in legal research. Much of the time spent on a research question goes into finding and screening material rather than analysing it and research usually ends when time runs out rather than when every relevant authority has been read. items.summary: The Supreme Court has held that the State government, which is legally entrusted with protecting temple properties, cannot itself take over such properties by way of a gift deed in the name of public interest or administrative convenience [K Ramalingam and Others v. Government of Tamil Nadu and Others]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe made the observation while holding that the transfer of land belonging to the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple in Tamil Nadu's Erode district to the State government for the construction of a Taluk Office was illegal. The Court observed that the State's responsibility as a custodian of religious properties did not give it the authority to acquire ownership of such properties. The case stemmed from an accident which happened on October 11 when a Mini Cooper driven by Sajeev at high speed hit a scooter carrying three youngsters on the Athani-Airport Road in Nedumbassery, killing all three. While two of them died on the spot, the third succumbed to injuries later. items.title: PIL in Calcutta High Court seeks double-side printing on A4 paper for pleadings in West Bengal courts
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Calcutta High Court seeking a uniform mandate for filing physical pleadings and documents in 75 GSM A4 paper in duplex (back-to-back) format in the High Court and other courts across West Bengal [Akash Sharma v. Registrar General, High Court at Calcutta and Another] . The PIL aims to lower paper consumption, printing services and costs and the physical bulk of court records. The case is listed for hearing on November 23. Calcutta High Court on February 22, 2021 had asked its administrative side to consider mandating use of A4 paper with double-side printing for pleadings and filings. However, the plea filed by advocate Akash Sharma states that further progress of the matter could not be ascertained through publicly available records or notices. This PIL primarily seeks to determine the outcome of the order dated February 22, 2021 and a fresh consideration of the matter to prescribe a uniform practice of using 75 GSM A4 paper in a duplex-printed format across all courts in the State.
